items.excerpt: EMBL scientists used AI to design NovoTags, small de novo protein tags that bind fluorescent dyes so researchers can track specific proteins inside living cells. An inducible variant, NovoSplit, acts as a molecular switch and could distinguish up to 30 proteins at once by combining emission spectrum and fluorescence lifetime.

Researchers developed an AI-enhanced rare-event sampling framework (AI+RES) that predicts the frequency of extreme heatwaves using up to 1000 times less compute than conventional climate modeling. The AI directs full physics-based models to simulate only the high-probability scenarios, bridging deep-learning efficiency with physical reliability.

Argonne National Laboratory released ChemGraph, an open-source framework that uses AI agents and large language models to automate computational chemistry and materials-science workflows. Researchers describe a problem in plain language and the system plans, runs, and analyzes the physics-based simulations for battery, combustion, and materials research.

A Rutgers-led team built an AI system that continuously monitors mouse locomotor activity and applies machine learning to flag health problems, detecting issues 3-5 days before obvious clinical signs appeared. The tool, reported in Lab Animal, aims to improve welfare and reliability in laboratory animal research.
